extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent practitioners, and patent examiners involved in USPTO appeal practice (appeal briefs, examiner’s answers, and related proceedings)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on preparing and filing appeal briefs in U.S. patent prosecution, handling amendments/evidence after appeal, and preparing/assessing the examiner's answer and appeal conference procedures before the Patent Trial and Appeal Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence appendix encouraged / identification of relied evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office strongly encourages and appreciates receiving copies of the evidence relied upon (e.g., copies of declarations and affidavits, evidence of secondary considerations, etc.). Alternatively, appellants should clearly identify in the appeal brief the evidence relied upon using a clear description of the evidence along with the date of entry of such evidence into the Image File Wrapper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing copies ensures the Board considers the proper evidence and avoids confusion about what the brief references. If not included, at minimum include clear description and the date the evidence entered the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Real party in interest statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeal brief must include a statement identifying by name the real party in interest at time the brief is filed, except when the named inventor(s) are the real party in interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identification allows the Board to comply with ethics/conflict-of-interest rules. Example wording: 'The real party in interest is XXXX corporation, the assignee of record, which is a subsidiary of a joint venture between YYYY corporation and ZZZZ corporation.' If omitted, the Office may assume the named inventor(s) are the real party in interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of related appeals, interferences, and trials
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeal brief should identify by application, patent, appeal, interference, or trial number all other prior or pending appeals, interferences, trials before the Board, or judicial proceedings that: involve an application or patent owned by the appellant or assignee; are known to appellant or representative; and may be related to, directly affect, or be directly affected by the Board’s decision in the pending appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there are no such related cases, the appellant need not include the statement; omission allows the Office to assume there are no related cases. The rule does not require copies of decisions in related cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary of claimed subject matter
rubrics_metrics.description: A concise explanation of the subject matter defined in each rejected independent claim must be provided, with references to the specification in the Record by page and line number or by paragraph number, and to the drawing by reference characters, if any.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For claims containing means-plus-function or step-plus-function (35 U.S.C. 112(f)), the brief must identify the structure, material, or acts in the specification corresponding to each claimed function (with specific references). Reference to the patent application publication alone does not satisfy this requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Argument content and structure requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Arguments must be presented for each ground of rejection and explain why the examiner erred, including citations to statutes, regulations, authorities, and parts of the Record relied on.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A statement that merely points out what a claim recites is not an argument for patentability. All arguments and authorities an appellant wishes the Board to consider for the present appeal should be included in the appeal brief (except limited exceptions under §§ 41.41, 41.47, 41.52). Arguments raised first at oral hearing are not normally entitled to consideration. Use separate headings for each ground of rejection; use subheadings to identify claims or claim subgroups being argued. Grouping claims without separate argument waives separate consideration of those grouped claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headings and claim-subheading requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each ground of rejection must be argued under a separate heading that clearly identifies the ground being contested; for claims argued separately or as subgroups, subheadings identifying claim numbers must be used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples provided for various grouping strategies (e.g., 'Rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102(a)(2) over U.S. Patent No. X' with subheadings 'Claims 1-3', 'Claim 4', etc.). To ensure separate consideration by the Board, the appellant must use subheadings for claims claimed to deserve separate consideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on including non-admitted amendments/affidavits/evidence in brief
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 41.37(c)(2) prohibits inclusion in a brief of any new or non-admitted amendment, affidavit, or other evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If appellant wishes review of the examiner’s refusal to admit an amendment/affidavit/evidence, the review is by petition to the Director under 37 CFR 1.181. The time for filing such a petition is based on the date the examiner refused entry, not the filing date of the brief. If an appellant files an amendment at the same time as a brief, it must be in a separate paper; an amendment under 41.33(b) may not be included in the brief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims appendix format and presentation
rubrics_metrics.description: An appendix containing a copy of the claims involved in the appeal must be provided. The claims copy should be a clean copy and should not include markings such as brackets or underlining except for reissue/reexamination as permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The claims copy should be double-spaced and the appendix should start on a new page. Specific MPEP and CFR references for reissue and reexamination claim presentation are noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggested appeal brief content/order (example format)
rubrics_metrics.description: An example brief should contain, each starting on a separate page: (A) Identification page; (B) Table of Contents; (C) Real party in interest; (D) Related appeals/interferences/trials; (E) Summary of claimed subject matter; (F) Argument; (G) Claims appendix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an illustrative format—appeal brief is compliant with 37 CFR 41.37(c)(1) so long as it includes items (i)–(v) in the order set forth and does not include prohibited material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Appeal Center compliance review and consequences of non-compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Timely filed appeal briefs are reviewed by the Patent Appeal Center for compliance with 37 CFR 41.37. If compliant or containing only minor informalities, the brief is accepted and forwarded; if non-compliant, the appellant receives a notice requiring a corrected brief within the time set in the notice to avoid dismissal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If appellant disagrees with a finding of noncompliance, a petition under 37 CFR 41.3 may be filed, but filing the petition does not toll the time to reply. The Patent Appeal Center determines compliance for corrected briefs as well; it will correspond directly with appellant on non-compliant brief issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Finality of Patent Appeal Center acceptance
rubrics_metrics.description: Once an appeal brief is accepted by the Board as in compliance with 37 CFR 41.37, the appeal brief will not later be held defective by the Patent Appeal Center or the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Board will not return or remand the application to the examiner for issues related to a non-compliant appeal brief. Examiners are not required to review appeal briefs for compliance with 37 CFR 41.37.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments filed after notice of appeal but before filing brief
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments filed after filing a notice of appeal and prior to the filing of a brief may be admitted as provided in 37 CFR 1.116.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A new amendment must be submitted in a separate paper; entry is not a matter of right. Admittable reasons include canceling claims, complying with form requirements, presenting rejected claims in better form for consideration on appeal, or amending spec/claims upon showing good and sufficient reasons why the amendment is necessary and was not earlier presented (37 CFR 41.33(a)). If denied entry, examiner uses PTOL-303 to notify applicant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments filed on or after filing brief — limited admissibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments filed on or after the date of filing a brief may be admitted only to (1) cancel claims where cancellation does not affect the scope of other pending claims, or (2) rewrite dependent claims into independent form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All other amendments filed after the date of filing an appeal brief will not be admitted except as permitted by specified CFR provisions (41.39(b)(1), 41.50(a)(2)(i), and 41.50(b)(1)). An amendment filed on the same date as a non-compliant brief is considered filed under 41.33(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rules and examples for rewriting dependent claims into independent form
rubrics_metrics.description: Rewriting dependent claims into independent form (permitted under 41.33(b)(2)) includes rewriting a dependent claim as independent by adding limitations of the parent claim(s), or rewriting an independent claim to incorporate a dependent claim and canceling the dependent claim while adjusting dependency of other claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such amendments must be filed before the expiration of the time period set forth in 37 CFR 90.3 to avoid cancellation of objected-to claims. Recommended that appellants rewrite dependent claims which were objected to solely because of dependency before appeal is forwarded to the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner notification forms for non-entry of amendments/evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner denies entry of an amendment or affidavit/evidence filed prior to a brief, use form PTOL-303 to notify applicant; if denial occurs after filing a brief, use PTOL-304.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These forms notify the applicant of non-entry and the reason for non-entry and are part of the required exam process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner obligations when indicating entry of an amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: If examiner indicates in an advisory action that an amendment will be entered, the examiner must state how the individual rejections in the final Office action will be impacted by entry of the amendment, except where the amendment merely cancels claims or rewrites dependent claims into independent form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an amendment clearly places the application in condition for allowance, the examiner may enter the amendment and allow the application. Examiners must respond to all amendments filed after an appeal has been taken and prior to transfer of jurisdiction to the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admission of affidavits or other evidence after notice of appeal but before brief
rubrics_metrics.description: An affidavit or other evidence filed after the date of filing a notice of appeal but prior to the filing of a brief may be admitted if the examiner determines that: (A) the affidavits/evidence overcomes all rejections under appeal; and (B) a showing of good and sufficient reasons why the evidence is necessary and was not earlier presented has been made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the examiner denies entry of such evidence, use PTOL-303 to notify applicant. If the evidence clearly places the application in condition for allowance, the examiner may enter it and allow the application. Otherwise, evidence filed after filing an appeal generally will not be admitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of Information Disclosure Statements after notice of appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Information Disclosure Statements (IDS) submitted after the date of a notice of appeal are normally held in abeyance pending a decision on the appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consideration of IDS is governed by MPEP § 609 and 37 CFR 1.97 and 1.98, not by 37 CFR 41.33.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner’s answer — grounds of rejection content and new/withdrawn rejections
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner’s answer should state every ground of rejection set forth in the Office action from which the appeal is taken (as modified) that is being maintained, list any withdrawn rejections under 'WITHDRAWN REJECTIONS,' and list any new grounds under 'NEW GROUNDS OF REJECTION.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A new ground of rejection must be clearly designated and, for each new ground, include a complete explanation with proper reference to statute, prior art relied upon, and claim numbers. An examiner’s answer including a new ground must be approved (signed) by the Director or delegated designee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner’s answer — response to appellant’s arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: The examiner’s answer must include a statement whether the examiner disagrees with each of appellant’s arguments and an explanation of reasons for any disagreement, using headings and subheadings paralleling the appellant’s brief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should furnish the appellant a written answer within two months after receipt of the brief. If the final rejection fully addresses the arguments, the examiner may use a simplified 'Response to Arguments' that refers to the final rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal conference requirement and participants
rubrics_metrics.description: An appeal conference is mandatory in all cases where an acceptable brief has been filed, unless the examiner (with SPE approval) concludes the appeal should not go forward.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Participants should include the examiner preparing the examiner’s answer, a supervisory patent examiner (SPE), and another experienced examiner (conferee). Conference should consider dropping cumulative art rejections and eliminating technical rejections of doubtful value. If rejections maintained, the responsible examiner prepares the examiner’s answer. The examiner’s answer must list 'Conferees:' with typed/printed names and their initials next to their names on the record to show the conference occurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation and approval for new grounds of rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: If the examiner’s answer contains a new ground of rejection, it must clearly designate the rejection as a new ground and be approved by the Director (or delegated TC Director/designee), with the approving signature included in the answer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent Appeal Center will review answers to confirm that an appeal conference was held and that required conferee information appears; it may return the application for corrective action if the indication is missing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appellant options and timing when examiner’s answer contains a new ground
rubrics_metrics.description: If an examiner's answer contains a new ground of rejection, appellant has two months from the date of the examiner’s answer to: (1) request prosecution be reopened (by filing a reply under § 1.111 with or without amendment or submission of affidavits/evidence) which will be treated as a request to withdraw the appeal; or (2) maintain the appeal by filing a reply brief under § 41.41 addressing each new ground (the reply brief may not be accompanied by any amendment, affidavit, or other evidence).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a reply brief is accompanied by any amendment or evidence, it will be treated as a request to reopen prosecution under paragraph (b)(1). Extensions of time under § 1.136(a) do not apply to the period set in this section; see specific CFR provisions for extensions elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing effects of examiner’s answer mailing date
rubrics_metrics.description: The mailing date of the examiner's answer begins the period for filing a reply brief (which transfers jurisdiction to the Board), the time to request an oral hearing, and the time period for payment of the appeal forwarding fee (unless a petition under 1.181 is filed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners should furnish answers within two months of receiving the brief; current procedures do not permit an appeal to proceed to the Board without an examiner’s answer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of claims and rejections absent appellant argument
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners must treat all pending, rejected claims as being on appeal and maintain all rejections set forth in the Office action unless appellant has overcome the rejection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where appellant failed to present any argument on a rejection or requested a rejection be held in abeyance, the examiner should maintain the rejection and identify that the appellant has not argued the rejection in the brief. The Board presumes all rejected claims are on appeal except those explicitly canceled by amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling non-English documents relied on by examiner
rubrics_metrics.description: If a document relied upon by the examiner is in a language other than English, a translation must be obtained so the record is clear as to the precise facts the examiner is relying upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The translation may be a machine translation or an English equivalent of the non-English document. See MPEP § 2120 for reliance upon abstracts and foreign language documents in support of a rejection.
